definitions: In telecommunications, the SINR (Signal-to-Interference-plus-Noise Ratio) is a measure of the quality of a wireless connection. It is defined as the power of a certain signal of interest divided by the sum of the interference power and the noise power.
A key metric used to determine the capacity and reliability of wireless communication systems.
examples: The SINR was too low for a stable connection.
Optimizing SINR is crucial for 5G networks.
We measured the SINR at various points in the building.
